contributions.parallelism: no explicit list; narrative contribution statement

evidence.quote: In this paper we present two different microachitectures for the computation of fused FP8 4-way dot product (DOT4) with scaling and accumulation to FP32 wthout any intermediate rounding.

• Compute-architecture selection: Through synthesis-backed evaluation under throughput-matched FP16/BF16/TF32 constraints, we show that dot-product units reduce area by 47%–55% and power by 25%–36% relative to multiplier– adder pipelines.
• Numerical-precision trade-offs: We characterize the feasible numeric region of the design space in terms of intermediate precision, accumulator precision, and stochastic rounding.

• Precision multiplexing strategies: We systematically analyze resource-sharing strategies and identify a clear unified–hybrid switching boundary in the area–power plane: fully unified all-in-one designs minimize area, whereas FP/INT-partitioned hybrid designs achieve better Pareto fronts once cross-family precision heterogeneity becomes sufficiently large.
We design a dot product-accumulate unit to support MXFP8 (E5M2, E4M3) data formats with 8-bit scales and an FP32 accumulator to minimize overflows and precision losses.
We introduce MXDOTP, a RISC-V ISA extension that fuses scaling and dot product into a single four-operand instruction.
We integrate MXDOTP into an 8-core Snitch cluster, reaching up to 80 % utilization.
